Statement I : On heating with ${KHSO}_{4}$, glycerol is dehydrated and acrolein is formed.

Statement II : Acrolein has fruity odour and can be used to test glycerol's presence.

Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: It is a colorless liquid with a piercing, acrid smell. The smell of burnt fat (as when cooking oil is heated to its smoke point) is caused by glycerol in the burning fat breaking down into acrolein. It does not have fruity smell so, statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following will be oxidized by $HI{O}_{4}$ ?

$1 .$ $R - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - R$

$2 .$ $R - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - R$

$3 .$ $R - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - C{H}_{2} - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - R$

$4 .$ $R - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - R$

Select the correct answer using the codes below
questions.solution:
The net result of oxidation is the cleavage of the bond between C's with the attached O's with addition of OH to 'C' of each $C - O$ .

In 1, 2-diols, the net effect is the oxidation is the cleavage of  bond and attachment of an OH to each 'C' atom. The gem-diol so formed loses a molecule of ${H}_{2}O$ .

$1 .$ $R - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - R\overset{HI{O}_{4}}{\to}R - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - OH + HO - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - R$

$2 .$ $R - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - R\overset{HI{O}_{4}}{\to}R - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - OH + O = CH - R$

$4 .$ $R - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - R\overset{HI{O}_{4}}{\to}R - CH = O + O = HCR$

Which of the following statements are correct with respect to benzene?
(i) It forms triozonide with $\mathrm{O}_3$.
(ii) It is non-planar.
(iii) It forms only one monosubstituted product with $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COCl}$ in the presence of anhyd. $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$.
(iv) If forms hexachlorobenzene on heating with $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ under photochemical condition.
questions.solution:
(ii) Benzene is a planar molecule. (iii) Benzene when treated with a mixture of ethanoyl chloride $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COCl}$ and aluminium chloride as catalyst. A ketone called phenyle thanone (monosubstituted) is obtained.
(iv) Benzene when heated with $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ under photochemical condition gives $1,2,3,4,5,6$-hexachlorocyclohexane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct for phenol?

(A) In general, phenol is more acidic than alcohol.

(B) Phenol is used in the production of melamine plastic.

(C) Phenol gives violet colour with neutral ferric chloride solution.

(D) Phenol when heated with acetyl chloride gives phenetole.
questions.solution: Phenol is more acidic than alcohols due to stabilisation of phenoxide ion through resonance. Melamine ( or formaldehyde melamine polymer) is obtained from condensation polymerisation of melamine with formaldehyde. Phenol reacts with neutral ${FeCl}_{3}$ solution to give violet colour complex which is soluble in water. When Phenol is treated with acetyl chloride it gives Phenylacetate. Phenylacetate is an ester.

questions.q: Match each of the compounds given in Column I with the reaction (s) that they can undergo, given in Column II.
questions.solution:
- A. 2-bromobenzofuran: This compound has an alkyl bromide group at a benzylic position. This functional group can undergo p. Nucleophilic substitution to replace the bromine and q. Elimination to form a double bond.
- B. Phenylethanol: This is an alcohol. Alcohols can react with acid anhydrides to form esters, which is an \(\mathrm{s}\). Esterification reaction. They can also be oxidized to aldehydes or ketones, a process that is also called t. Dehydrogenation.
- C. Salicylaldehyde: This compound has two functional groups: an aldehyde and a phenol. Aldehydes are known to undergo r. Nucleophilic addition. The phenolic hydroxyl group can be esterified with acetic anhydride, which is an \(\mathrm{s}\). Esterification reaction.
- D. 2-bromo-4-nitrophenol: This compound is a brominated phenol with a nitro group. The bromine atom on the aromatic ring, activated by the strong electron-withdrawing nitro group, can undergo p. Nucleophilic substitution (specifically, nucleophilic aromatic substitution). The phenolic hydroxyl group can be oxidized, a form of t. Dehydrogenation.

(b)C_6 H_{12} O_6 $\xrightarrow{ zymase }$(q)$CH_3-OH

$\xrightarrow[443 K]{ConcH_2 SO_4}$ \end{aligned}$(r)C_2 H_5 OH+CO_2

questions.solution:
Short reasoning:
- (a) \($\mathrm{CO}+$2 $\mathrm{H}}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}$}_{3} $\mathrm{OH}$\) (methanol) over \($\mathrm{ZnO}-\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}$}_{3} $\rightarrow \mathrm{q}$\).
- (b) \($\mathrm{C}}_{6}  \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}$}_{6}\)-Zymase \( → \) ethanol \(+$\mathrm{CO}}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{r}\).
- (c) Ethanol + conc. \(\mathrm{H}$}_{2} $\mathrm{SO}}_{4}\) at \(443  \mathrm{~K} \rightarrow\) dehydration to alkene \(\left(\mathrm{CH}$}_{2}=$\mathrm{CH}}_{2}\right) \rightarrow \mathrm{s}\).
- (d) Ethanol + conc. \(\mathrm{H}$}_{2} $\mathrm{SO}}_{4}\) at \(413  \mathrm{~K} \rightarrow\) etherification to diethyl ether \( $\left(\mathrm{C}$}_{2} $\mathrm{H}}_{5}- \mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}$}_{2}  \mathrm{H}$}_{5}\right)$\rightarrow \mathrm{p}$\).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reaction of 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol with $\text{HBr}$ gives 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product.
Reason (R): The reaction involves a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol (neopentyl alcohol) is a highly sterically hindered primary alcohol. Upon reaction with $\text{HBr}$, the $-\text{OH}$ group is protonated to form a good leaving group ($-\text{OH}_2^+$).

Due to the high instability of a primary carbocation, the departure of the water molecule is accompanied by a simultaneous 1,2-methyl shift from the adjacent quaternary carbon. This rearrangement directly yields a more stable tertiary carbocation (tert-pentyl carbocation).

The nucleophilic bromide ion ($\text{Br}^-$) then attacks this tertiary carbocation to form 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol is treated with concentrated $HBr$, the major product formed is:
questions.solution:
The reaction proceeds via an $S_N1$ mechanism involving a carbocation intermediate.

Step 1: Protonation of the alcohol followed by the loss of a water molecule generates a secondary carbocation at C-2.
$CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH(OH)-CH_3 \xrightarrow{H^+} CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH^+-CH_3 + H_2O$

Step 2: The less stable secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift from the adjacent quaternary carbon (C-3) to form a more stable tertiary carbocation.
$CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH^+-CH_3 \xrightarrow{\text{1,2-methyl shift}} CH_3-C^+(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$

Step 3: Nucleophilic attack by the bromide ion ($Br^-$) on the tertiary carbocation yields the major product, 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane.
$CH_3-C^+(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3 + Br^- \rightarrow CH_3-C(Br)(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$

Direct substitution without rearrangement would give 2-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane, which is a minor product.

Answer: 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane

Assertion (A): Chlorobenzene cannot be converted to phenol by boiling with aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ at standard temperature and pressure.
Reason (R): In chlorobenzene, the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond acquires a partial double bond character due to resonance, making it difficult to cleave.

(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. Aryl halides like chlorobenzene are extremely less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reactions under normal conditions. The conversion of chlorobenzene to phenol (Dow's process) requires drastic conditions: $623\text{ K}$ temperature and $300\text{ atm}$ pressure.

This resonance imparts a partial double bond character to the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond. As a result, the bond cleavage in chlorobenzene is much more difficult than in alkyl halides, rendering it unreactive towards aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ at standard temperature and pressure.

Hence, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Cumene on aerial oxidation followed by subsequent acid hydrolysis yields an aromatic product 'A' and an aliphatic byproduct 'B'. Which of the following chemical tests will give a positive result for the aromatic product 'A'?
questions.solution:
The commercial preparation of phenol involves the aerial oxidation of cumene (isopropylbenzene) to form cumene hydroperoxide, which upon subsequent acid hydrolysis yields phenol as the aromatic product 'A' and acetone as the aliphatic byproduct 'B'.

Phenol contains a phenolic $-OH$ group, which can be identified by the neutral ferric chloride ($FeCl_3$) test, producing a characteristic violet coloration.

The iodoform test would be positive for the aliphatic byproduct (acetone), not the aromatic product. Phenol does not respond to the Lucas test (which is for aliphatic alcohols) or Tollen's test (which is for aldehydes).

Answer: Neutral ferric chloride test

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkene 'A' undergoes acid-catalysed hydration to yield a major product 'B'. When 'B' is treated with Lucas reagent, it produces immediate turbidity at room temperature. Identify the alkene 'A'.
questions.solution:
The production of immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent (concentrated $\mathrm{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\mathrm{ZnCl_2}$) at room temperature is a characteristic test for tertiary alcohols. Therefore, the major product 'B' must be a tertiary alcohol.

Acid-catalysed hydration of alkenes follows Markovnikov's rule, where the $\mathrm{OH}$ group attaches to the more substituted carbon atom of the double bond.

Let us evaluate the hydration products of the given alkenes:
Propene yields propan-2-ol (a secondary alcohol).
But-1-ene yields butan-2-ol (a secondary alcohol).
Ethene yields ethanol (a primary alcohol).
2-Methylpropene yields 2-methylpropan-2-ol (a tertiary alcohol).

Since 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol, it will give immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent. Thus, the starting alkene 'A' is 2-methylpropene.

Answer: 2-Methylpropene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the commercial preparation of phenol, a specific aromatic hydrocarbon is oxidized in the presence of air to form a hydroperoxide intermediate. This intermediate, upon subsequent treatment with dilute acid, yields phenol and acetone as the final products. Identify the starting aromatic hydrocarbon.
questions.solution:
The commercial preparation of phenol yielding acetone as a valuable by-product is known as the cumene process.

The starting material for this process is cumene, which is the common name for isopropylbenzene. It is oxidized in the presence of air to form cumene hydroperoxide at the benzylic position. This intermediate is then converted to phenol and acetone by treating it with dilute acid.

n-Propylbenzene, ethylbenzene, and toluene do not form cumene hydroperoxide and would not yield acetone upon oxidation and subsequent hydrolysis.

Answer: Isopropylbenzene

Working backwards from the final product:

Benzenesulfonic acid ('Y') is formed by treating the starting compound 'X' with oleum (sulfonation). Therefore, the starting aromatic compound 'X' must be benzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound on treatment with a few drops of neutral ferric chloride solution produces a characteristic violet coloration. The functional group present in the compound is :
questions.solution:
The neutral ferric chloride ($FeCl_3$) test is a characteristic qualitative test used for the identification of the phenolic functional group.

When a phenol is treated with a few drops of neutral $FeCl_3$ solution, it forms a colored iron-phenol coordination complex, which imparts a characteristic violet, blue, or green coloration to the solution.

Aliphatic alcohols do not react with neutral $FeCl_3$. Carboxylic acids typically give a buff or reddish-brown precipitate, while aldehydes do not respond to this test.

Answer: Phenolic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reactions of 3-methylpentan-2-ol:
Reaction 1: Treatment with $HBr$ yields major product A.
Reaction 2: Treatment with $SOCl_2$ yields major product B.

Identify the IUPAC names of products A and B.
questions.solution:
Reaction 1 (with $HBr$): The reaction proceeds via a carbocation intermediate. Protonation and loss of water from 3-methylpentan-2-ol forms a secondary carbocation at C-2. A 1,2-hydride shift occurs from C-3 to C-2 to form a more stable tertiary carbocation. Nucleophilic attack by $Br^-$ yields 3-bromo-3-methylpentane as the major product (A).

Reaction 2 (with $SOCl_2$): The reaction of alcohols with thionyl chloride ($SOCl_2$) follows an $S_Ni$ (or $S_N2$ in the presence of a base) mechanism. This mechanism does not involve a free carbocation intermediate, so no carbocation rearrangement occurs. The $-OH$ group is directly replaced by $-Cl$ at the same position, yielding 2-chloro-3-methylpentane as the major product (B).

Answer: A = 3-bromo-3-methylpentane, B = 2-chloro-3-methylpentane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The commercial preparation of phenol from cumene is highly significant because it yields two valuable products, phenol and acetone, in large quantities.
Reason (R): The intermediate cumene hydroperoxide undergoes acid-catalyzed cleavage to produce exactly one molecule of phenol and one molecule of acetone.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because the cumene process is the preferred commercial method for manufacturing phenol, largely due to the simultaneous production of acetone, which is also a highly valuable solvent and chemical intermediate.

Reason (R) is correct and explains (A). The oxidation of cumene yields cumene hydroperoxide. When this intermediate is treated with dilute acid, it undergoes cleavage such that every molecule of the hydroperoxide yields one molecule of phenol and one molecule of acetone. This 1:1 stoichiometric cleavage is the direct reason why acetone is obtained in large quantities alongside phenol.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): tert-Butyl alcohol produces turbidity immediately with Lucas reagent at room temperature, whereas n-butyl alcohol does not.

Reason (R): Primary alcohols undergo $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions faster than tertiary alcohols.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect.
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: Lucas reagent is a mixture of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$. Tertiary alcohols like tert-butyl alcohol react immediately to produce turbidity (due to the formation of an insoluble alkyl chloride), while primary alcohols like n-butyl alcohol do not produce turbidity at room temperature.

Reason (R) is correct: In general, primary substrates undergo $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions faster than tertiary substrates due to less steric hindrance.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The reaction of alcohols with Lucas reagent proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism, which involves the formation of a carbocation intermediate. Tertiary alcohols react fastest because they form highly stable tertiary carbocations. The $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactivity order does not explain the Lucas test observations.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

B. 3-Methylbutan-2-ol + $\text{PBr}_3$II. 1-Bromopropane

questions.solution:
The reaction of alcohols with $\text{PBr}_3$ generally proceeds without the formation of a free carbocation, so no rearrangement occurs. In contrast, the reaction of secondary and branched primary alcohols with $\text{HBr}$ proceeds via carbocation intermediates, which can undergo rearrangement to form more stable carbocations.

A. Propan-1-ol reacts with $\text{PBr}_3$ to give 1-bromopropane directly (A - II).

B. 3-Methylbutan-2-ol reacts with $\text{PBr}_3$ without rearrangement to give 2-bromo-3-methylbutane (B - III).

C. 2-Methylpropan-1-ol (isobutyl alcohol) reacts with $\text{HBr}$ to form a primary oxonium ion, which undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift as water leaves, forming a stable tertiary butyl carbocation. This gives 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (C - IV).

D. 2-Methylbutan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol. It reacts with $\text{HBr}$ to form a stable tertiary carbocation directly, yielding 2-bromo-2-methylbutane (D - I).

Thus, the correct match is A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I.

Answer: A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Isopropylbenzene is oxidized in the presence of air followed by treatment with dilute acid to yield an aromatic compound Y and an aliphatic compound Z. When compound Y is treated with concentrated nitric acid, it forms a product W. The product W is:
questions.solution:
Isopropylbenzene (cumene) is oxidized in the presence of air to form cumene hydroperoxide, which upon treatment with dilute acid yields phenol (aromatic compound Y) and acetone (aliphatic compound Z).

When phenol is treated with concentrated nitric acid, it undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution at all ortho and para positions to form 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) as the product W.

Using dilute nitric acid would yield a mixture of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol, whereas concentrated nitric acid yields the trinitro product.

Answer: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown alcohol with the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ is treated with Lucas reagent at room temperature. It produces turbidity immediately. The IUPAC name of the unknown alcohol is:
questions.solution:
The Lucas test is used to distinguish primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols. The reagent is a mixture of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$.

The formation of turbidity is due to the formation of an insoluble alkyl chloride. Tertiary alcohols react immediately to form turbidity, secondary alcohols take about 5 minutes, and primary alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature.

Since the unknown alcohol ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) produces turbidity immediately, it must be a tertiary alcohol.

Among the structural isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$:
Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol.
Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol.
2-Methylpropan-1-ol is a primary alcohol.
2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol.

Therefore, the unknown alcohol is 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

Answer: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol

Therefore, the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Commercially, carboxylic acids are directly reduced to primary alcohols using lithium aluminium hydride ($\text{LiAlH}_4$).
Reason (R): $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is an expensive reagent, hence commercially acids are first converted to esters and then catalytically reduced with hydrogen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false. Lithium aluminium hydride ($\text{LiAlH}_4$) is an excellent reducing agent, but it is highly expensive. Therefore, it is used only for preparing special chemicals and not for the large-scale commercial reduction of carboxylic acids to alcohols.

Reason (R) is true. Because of the high cost of $\text{LiAlH}_4$, the commercial method involves first converting the carboxylic acid to an ester (by reacting with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst), followed by catalytic hydrogenation ($\text{H}_2$/catalyst) of the ester to yield the primary alcohol.

Thus, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown alcohol produces turbidity with Lucas reagent in approximately 5 minutes at room temperature. Which of the following could be the alcohol?
questions.solution:
The Lucas test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols based on their reactivity with Lucas reagent (concentrated $\mathrm{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\mathrm{ZnCl_2}$).

Tertiary alcohols react immediately to form an insoluble alkyl chloride, producing immediate turbidity.

Secondary alcohols react slower, producing turbidity in approximately 5 minutes.

Primary alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature.

Since the unknown alcohol produces turbidity in 5 minutes, it must be a secondary alcohol. Among the given options, propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. Propan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-1-ol are primary alcohols, while 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol.

Answer: Propan-2-ol

questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the industrial preparation of phenol from cumene:
I. Cumene is prepared by the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with propene.
II. Cumene is oxidised in the presence of air to form cumene hydroperoxide.
III. The conversion of cumene hydroperoxide to phenol and acetone is carried out by treating it with a strong base.
IV. Acetone is obtained in large quantities as a valuable by-product in this method.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is typically prepared by the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with propene.

Statement II is correct: In the commercial preparation of phenol, cumene is oxidised in the presence of air to form cumene hydroperoxide.

Statement III is incorrect: The cleavage of cumene hydroperoxide to yield phenol and acetone is achieved by treating it with dilute acid ($\text{H}^+$), not a strong base.

Statement IV is correct: Acetone is a major by-product of this reaction and is obtained in large quantities, making the process economically highly viable.

Therefore, exactly three statements (I, II, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only three

Consider the following sequence of reactions:

Aniline $\xrightarrow[\text{0-5 }^{\circ}\text{C}]{\text{NaNO}_2 \text{ + HCl}}$ Intermediate $\xrightarrow{\text{Warm H}_2\text{O}}$ Compound X $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2\text{ (aq)}}$ Compound Y

Identify Compound Y and its physical appearance.
questions.solution:
Aniline reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^{\circ}\text{C}$ to undergo diazotisation, forming benzene diazonium chloride.

Warming the diazonium salt with water hydrolyses it to form phenol (Compound X).

When phenol is treated with aqueous bromine (bromine water), it undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution at all ortho and para positions due to the strong activating effect of the $-\text{OH}$ group in aqueous medium. This results in the formation of 2,4,6-tribromophenol (Compound Y), which appears as a white precipitate.

Answer: 2,4,6-Tribromophenol, white precipitate

Read the following statements regarding the chemical reactions of phenol:

Statement I: Oxidation of phenol with chromic acid produces a conjugated diketone.
Statement II: Heating phenol with zinc dust yields benzene.
Statement III: Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol yields salicylic acid as the major product.
Statement IV: Kolbe's reaction involves the electrophilic attack of carbon dioxide on the phenoxide ion.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: Oxidation of phenol with chromic acid ($\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) produces benzoquinone, which is a conjugated diketone.

Statement II is correct: Phenol is reduced to benzene when heated with zinc dust.

Statement III is incorrect: Reimer-Tiemann reaction involves the treatment of phenol with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide, followed by acidification, to yield salicylaldehyde as the major product, not salicylic acid.

Statement IV is correct: In Kolbe's reaction, the phenoxide ion is highly reactive towards electrophilic aromatic substitution and undergoes attack by carbon dioxide (a weak electrophile) to form salicylic acid.

Therefore, three statements (I, II, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only three

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reaction of phenol with bromine in $\text{CS}_{2}$ at low temperature yields a mixture of ortho and para bromophenols.

Reason (R): In aqueous medium, phenol ionizes to form the phenoxide ion, which is highly activating towards electrophilic aromatic substitution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: Phenol reacts with bromine in non-polar solvents like $\text{CS}_{2}$ at low temperature ($273\text{ K}$) to give a mixture of ortho and para bromophenols. This is a monosubstitution reaction.

Reason (R) is correct: In aqueous medium, phenol ionizes to form the phenoxide ion. The phenoxide ion is much more activating than the $-\text{OH}$ group towards electrophilic aromatic substitution, leading to the formation of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

However, Reason (R) explains the polysubstitution reaction in aqueous medium, not the monosubstitution in $\text{CS}_{2}$. The correct explanation for Assertion (A) is that in non-polar solvents, the ionization of phenol is suppressed, and the $-\text{OH}$ group is less activating.

Thus, both Assertion and Reason are correct, but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

Consider the following sequence of reactions:

$\text{Benzene} \xrightarrow{\text{Oleum}} \text{A} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) }\text{H}^+]{\text{(i) }\text{NaOH, } \Delta} \text{B} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2\text{ / H}_2\text{O}} \text{C}$

The final product 'C' is:
questions.solution:
Benzene reacts with oleum (fuming sulfuric acid) to undergo sulfonation, forming benzenesulfonic acid (Compound A).

Benzenesulfonic acid is fused with sodium hydroxide at high temperature to form sodium phenoxide, which upon acidification ($\text{H}^+$) yields phenol (Compound B).

Phenol reacts with bromine water ($\text{Br}_2\text{ / H}_2\text{O}$), a highly polar medium. The strong activating effect of the $-\text{OH}$ group in the polar solvent leads to rapid polyhalogenation, forming a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol (Compound C).

If the reaction were carried out in a non-polar solvent like $\text{CS}_2$, $p$-bromophenol would be the major product.

Answer: 2,4,6-Tribromophenol

questions.q: An alkene, 2-methylpropene, is subjected to acid-catalysed hydration to yield a major product 'A'. When a small amount of product 'A' is treated with Lucas reagent at room temperature, what visual observation is expected?
options: No turbidity is observed at room temperature
A blood red colour is produced immediately
questions.solution:
Acid-catalysed hydration of 2-methylpropene follows Markovnikov's rule, where the hydroxyl group attaches to the more substituted carbon of the double bond. This yields 2-methylpropan-2-ol as the major product 'A'.

2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol.

Lucas reagent is a mixture of concentrated $\mathrm{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\mathrm{ZnCl}_2$. Tertiary alcohols react very rapidly with Lucas reagent to form insoluble alkyl chlorides, which results in the immediate appearance of turbidity at room temperature.

Answer: Turbidity appears immediately

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{alc. KOH}} Y \xrightarrow[(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO})_2\text{O}_2]{\text{HBr}} Z$
questions.solution:
Reaction of primary alcohol with $\text{PCl}_5$ gives alkyl chloride, $\text{POCl}_3$, and $\text{HCl}$.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{PCl}_5 \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$

Thus, $X = \text{POCl}_3$.

Dehydrohalogenation of 1-chloropropane with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ yields propene.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$

Thus, $Y = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$.

Addition of $\text{HBr}$ to propene in the presence of peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov addition.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO})_2\text{O}_2} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$

Thus, $Z = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$.

Answer: $X = \text{POCl}_3$; $Z = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The functional group that can be identified through phthalein dye test is :
questions.solution:
The phthalein dye test is a characteristic test used for the identification of the phenolic functional group.

When a phenol is heated with phthalic anhydride in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid, it undergoes a condensation reaction to form a colorless compound, phenolphthalein.

Upon adding an alkaline solution like dilute sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to this mixture, a characteristic pink or red color is produced due to the formation of the phenolphthalein anion.

Therefore, the functional group identified through the phthalein dye test is phenolic.

Answer: Phenolic

questions.q: Identify A and B
questions.solution: Ether when treated with $HI$ produces both benzyl iodide or phenol. Under acidic conditions (i.e., with a small amount of HI), the ether can undergo an acid-catalyzed cleavage to form phenol and benzyl iodide. In this reaction, the $HI$ acts as a catalyst, and the protonation of the ether oxygen atom makes it a good leaving group, which then departs to form benzyl carbocation. The carbocation can then react with the iodide ion to form benzyl iodide, while the protonated oxygen atom can undergo deprotonation and form phenol.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The acidic strength of mono substituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.

Statement II: $o$-nitrophenol, $m$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.solution:
The presence of the Nitro group in the ortho or para position decreases the electron density in the $- OH$ bond. As a result, it is easier to lose a proton from mono substituted nitro phenol Hence, ortho and para nitrophenols are stronger acids than phenol.

The acidic nature of nitrophenols increases in the order: meta $<$ ortho $<$ para.

Meta position shows only -I effect. Hence, it is less acidic than the para and ortho isomers.

Between para and ortho nitrophenols, para is more acidic due to the presence of an intramolecular hydrogen bonding that locks hydrogen of $- OH$ bond in ortho isomer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Anisole on cleavage with $\text{HI}$ gives
questions.solution:
Anisole is methoxy benzene. Anisole reacts with protons from hydroiodic acid to form methyl(phenyl) oxonium ion.
In the methyl(phenyl)oxonium ion, the oxygen atom has a positive charge. This positive charge is delocalised through resonance with the benzene ring. Due to this, the bond between the oxygen atom and the aromatic carbon atom of benzene has a partial double bond character. This bond is difficult to break. Hence, the iodide ion does not attack the aromatic carbon atom of the benzene ring. On the other hand, the bond between the oxygen atom and the carbon atom of the methyl group is a single bond. This bond can be easily broken.
Hence, the iodide ion attacks the carbon atom of the methyl group to form phenol and iodomethane.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about primary amines is false ?
options: Alkyl amines are stronger bases than aryl amines
Alkyl amines react with nitrous acid to produce alcohols
Aryl amines react with nitrous acid to produce phenols
Alkyl amines are stronger bases than ammonia
questions.solution:
Key Idea (i) Presence of electron withdrawing substituent decreases the basicity while the presence of electron releasing substituent like, $-\mathrm{CH}_3,-\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5$ etc increases the acidity.
(ii) $\mathrm{HNO}_2$ converts $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group of aliphatic amine into $-\mathrm{OH}$ while that of aromatic amines into $-\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{NCl}$.
Since, phenyl group is a electron withdrawing group, it decreases the basicity. Alkyl group, on the other hand, being electron releasing, increases the basicity. Thus, alkyl amines are more basic as compared to aryl amines as well as ammonia.
$$
\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{NH}_2 \stackrel{\mathrm{HNO}_2}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{OH}
$$
Thus, $\mathrm{HNO}_2$ (nitrous acid) converts alkyl amines to alcohols.
But $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{NH}_2 \stackrel{\mathrm{HNO}_2}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{~N}=\mathrm{NCl}$
benzene diazonium chloride
Thus, $\mathrm{HNO}_2$ does not convert aryl amines into phenol.

questions.solution:
Lucas test will be given by all the given alcohols within 5 minutes as all are $2^{\circ}$ alcohols. Exact structure can be known by molecular mass or formula of alcohol which will be obtained as follows :
Let molecular mass of alcohol be $M$.

The general formula of alcohols is $\mathrm{C}_n \mathrm{H}_{2 n+1} \mathrm{OH}$. The molecular mass 88 corresponds to the value of $n=5$. Thus, the $2^{\circ}$ alcohol is $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{CHCHOHCH}_3$.

questions.solution: When mixed ethers are used, the alkyl iodide produced depends on the nature of alkyl groups. If one group is Me and the other a pri- or sec-alkyl group, then methyl iodide is produced. Here reaction occurs via \($\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2\) mechanism$ and because of the steric effect of the larger group, \(\mathrmI^{-}\)attacks the smaller (Me) group. \(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OC}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}+ \mathrm{HI} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{OH} When the $substrate is a methyl \(t\)-alkyl ether, the products are \(t-R \mathrm{I} and \(\mathrm{MeOH}. Here reaction occurs by \($\mathrm{S}_${\mathrm{N}}$1\) mechanism and formation of $products is controlled by the stability of carbocation. Since carbocation stability order is \(3^{{}^{\circ}} \gt 2^{{}^{\circ}} \gt 1^{{}^{\circ}} \gt \stackrel{\$oplus}{$\mathrm{CH}_{3}$}\). \(\therefore \quad\) Alkyl halide is always derived$ from tert-alkyl group.

questions.q: Which one of the following compounds is most acidic?
questions.solution: Phenols are much more acidic than alcohols, due to the stabilisation of phenoxide ion by resonance. Phenoxide ion is stabilized due to following resonating structures : While in alcohols Ortho nitrophenol is most acidic because in it $-\mathrm{NO}_2$ electron attracting group is attached on ortho position which helps in stabilising of negative charge on the oxygen of phenoxide ion. Hence, due to this reason acidic character of phenol is increased, while on attachment of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group (electron donating group) acidic strength of phenol is decreased in cresol due to destabilisation of phenoxide ion.
